repository.title: MATLAB Tool Discovery Lab
repository.description: Study MATLAB tools and learn to compare step-response assumptions, numerical methods and control models before adoption.
repository.summary: A forked resource directory for MATLAB software, toolboxes, and learning materials. A second-order response explorer connects model behavior to tool-selection questions.
repository.audience: Students and engineers selecting MATLAB resources for a reproducible numerical task.

model.equation: y″ + 2ζωₙy′ + ωₙ²y = Kωₙ²r. Closed-form unit-step response is evaluated for underdamped, critical, and overdamped regimes.
assumptions: A linear time-invariant second-order system starts at rest.
No transport delay, saturation, sensor noise, or discrete controller is represented.
Overshoot is relative to the final K·r level; tracking error remains relative to the requested r.
The directory is a fork of mikecroucher/awesome-MATLAB and keeps its CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 license.
Linked tools have independent versions, dependencies, and licenses; listing does not establish suitability or maintenance.
The toy system has no hardware plant, converter, sensor, or measured parameter identification.
model.introduction: The browser solves a small analytic second-order system. It does not execute MATLAB or any linked toolbox; the response is a common example for deciding what capabilities to investigate.

modules.title: Translate a question into a tool requirement
modules.objective: Connect a model equation and expected outputs to the relevant resource category.
steps: Read the directory categories for learning, optimization, model reduction, and figure creation.
Apply the unit-gain response with damping 0.5 and natural frequency 1 rad/s.
Run to 20 seconds and distinguish tracking error from theoretical overshoot.
modules.reflection: Would solving this closed-form teaching problem require a specialist toolbox? What feature would justify one?

modules.title: Compare numerical behavior before features
modules.objective: Identify how damping changes the response while the requested target stays fixed.
steps: Keep the target, frequency, and gain fixed.
Change damping to 0.2 and predict a larger or smaller overshoot before running.
Use the plot to frame a concrete example you could reproduce in a candidate MATLAB tool.
modules.reflection: Why is a screenshot of a curve insufficient to compare solvers unless initial conditions and parameter values are included?

modules.title: Check a limiting case
modules.objective: Use critical damping as an analytic reference for a tool evaluation.
steps: Set damping to 1 while retaining unit gain and 1 rad/s natural frequency.
Predict the absence of overshoot and run to the fixed horizon.
Record the equation, units, and tolerances that a MATLAB reproduction should satisfy.

checkpoints.label: Critical damping has zero theoretical overshoot

modules.reflection: How would an analytic reference case help you decide whether an apparent difference is a solver issue or a configuration issue?

modules.title: Package a reviewable resource recommendation
modules.objective: Include model scope, dependencies, reproducibility, and license in a recommendation.
steps: Use damping 0.7, frequency 1.5 rad/s, and gain 0.8.
Predict the nonzero steady-state tracking error before running.
Read Contributing.md and license.md; describe the candidate tool with its own terms and a minimal reproduction plan.
modules.reflection: Write a recommendation that distinguishes a directory citation, a tool capability claim, and a result you personally reproduced.

source.scope: This browser lab is a standalone teaching approximation. Use the linked source for the project implementation.
